Key Activities: Plans and directs economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and develops new methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyse, present and extend the application of divisional statistics and prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.

Provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users (e.g. academics, policy makers, international bodies, etc.) and other professionals on the results of research and analytical studies, economic / social science theories and principles and advanced survey concepts and methods.
Plans and coordinates the development, collection, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical information for unique, complex and non-recurring policy studies.

Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients, assessing the impact on divisional programs and developing options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.
Supervises a unit or multi-disciplinary project teams responsible for statistical research projects and studies; manages the financial resources attached to each project.
Represents departmental interests when presenting analytical research and modelling studies to a variety of stakeholders.

1. Decision making: Plans and directs economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research covering multiple areas, industrial sectors, population segments or geographical areas.

Assesses client requirements for statistical information; recommends the conduct of special studies; defines project objectives and scope; selects and evaluates research standards and techniques to be used in the conduct of studies and in the reporting of findings as well as the analytical techniques and quantitative analytical methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data.
Determines priorities for specific studies and provides expert advice and recommendations to senior management on the significant issues affecting the sector’s policies and programs.
Develops modifications to program content and coverage and devises new methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics.
Conducts comprehensive research and analysis into socio-economic policy issues and recommends the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the Sector.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit responsible for statistical research projects and studies and leads multi-disciplinary project teams involved in special research projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of the programs. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications. Negotiates with suppliers for cost reductions/discounts.
3. Communication: Chairs meetings with professionals from research groups, other departments or levels of government to discuss current trends and developments, to acquire up-to-date knowledge of results, regulations and policies relating to socio-economic programs, and to develop consensus on the significant issues and priorities affecting the sector’s policies and programs.

Provides expert advice and recommendations to senior management on the significant issues affecting the sector’s policies and programs and submits program proposals and initiatives addressing the areas of concern to the Sector.

Interprets and adapts complex statistical data and information to provide decision-makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics with expertise leading to decision making regarding a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and initiatives
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: In-depth knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theories as they relate to a specialized area to plan the conduct of comprehensive research and analysis into socio-economic policy issues and to recommend the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the Sector.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices which are used in the development, collection, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data, in order to plan, develop, direct and undertake a research program.
Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and to provide technical advice to other professionals.
Writing and editing skills to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices related to project management, human resources and financial management in order to plan projects/studies, manage staff, (either directly or within a matrix management environment) and administer a budget.

Knowledge of existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work in order to plan, develop and direct a program of detailed analysis, evaluation and research, to improve existing data, develop new methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data, develop new concepts and extend the application of divisional statistics. Knowledge is also required of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to identify potential sources of information for special studies, to evaluate possible data conflicts, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.
5. Contextual knowledge: In-depth knowledge of the subject-matter area and of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine priorities for specific studies and to provide expert advice and recommendations to senior management on the significant issues affecting the sector’s policies and programs.

Knowledge of data users and suppliers from various levels of government and the private sector, to provide expert advice on study or survey results, negotiate or discuss data reporting agreements and ensure understanding or their needs.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labour, Prices, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc., to understand needs for new data, analyze the data and assess their impact on the area of specialization and share expertise with international organizations.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses and integrates data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses), evaluates the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other programs, develops modifications to program content and coverage and devises new survey methods, concepts, definitions and operational procedures.

Conducts comprehensive research and analysis into socio-economic policy issues, identifies significant issues affecting the sector’s policies and programs and recommends the development of policies, strategies and program initiatives addressing the areas of concern to the Sector.

Synthesizes complex statistical data and information from a wide range of sources to provide decision-makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics with expertise leading to decision making regarding a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and initiatives

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions. It is necessary to understand and interpret present policy issues and the socio-economic conditions of Canadians.

Education: Graduation with a degree from a recognized post secondary institution with acceptable specialization in economics, sociology or statistics.
Experience: Extensive and relevant subject matter experience developing or revising classifications, conceptual frameworks or metadata related to statistical outputs.
Extensive and relevant subject matter experience analyzing data for data validation, data integration or analytical publications.
Extensive and relevant experience managing a complex project or statistical process related to production, analysis or dissemination using statistical methods to produce outputs.
Recent and significant experience using programming languages and tools such as Python, R, SAS, SPSS or SQL for data analysis.
Competencies: Showing initiative and being action oriented
Abilities: Ability to manage a large project
Ability to identify and resolve problems
Ability to communicate effectively in writing
